newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates flat to lower in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates flat to lower in quiet market.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were steady to slightly weaker across the board on Thursday in a generally quiet market, brokers said.

They said a combination of the absence of many key players due to a week of industry functions in London, a lacklustre physical crude market and refinery turnarounds in the Far East made for a quiet market.
"There's very little fixing going on," said one broker. "But I expect once people get back to their desks after IP week it will pick up again,."
Rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) on trips from the Middle East to Japan had eased to around W59 against W60-62.5 on Wednesday.
While rates for trips from the Middle East to Singapore remained around W47.5.
The Mediterranean was slightly weaker with rates for 80,000 tonners on cross-Med trips ranging W80-85, while 130,000 tonners commanded around W100-105.
Rates in the UK/Cont sector were around W115 for promptish lifting and W107-110 further out.
There was continued interest in the sector for vessels going Transatlantic. Brokers said a 250,000 tonner could command roughly W65-70 while a 130 tonne vessel would fetch roughly W95.
In the Western Hemisphere, fixing activity picked up but this had not yet done much to boost rates with 70,000 tonners on up U.S. coast trips commanding around W115-120.
